Odaily星球日报讯 与中国知名量化机构鸣石投资相关的 Jupiter Research Capital 旗下基金在 AI 相关股票大跌期间遭遇重创，7 月以来短短三周多时间内净值下跌超过 40%。

投资者更新数据显示，该基金 7 月初前三个交易日亏损不足 7.5%，但截至 7 月 24 日亏损扩大至约 43%。该基金今年早些时候管理规模约 1.86 亿美元，采用市场中性策略，并使用 2-4 倍杠杆。

近期，随着市场对 AI 投资可持续性的担忧升温，全球 AI 产业链股票大幅回调，重仓 AI 主题的对冲基金普遍承压。高盛称，中国市场出现“量化地震”，动量策略反转导致 AI 和小盘股相关仓位遭遇平仓压力。（BloomBerg）
original_text:
AI Boom Lures Crypto Capital, But $2.7 Billion Firm Holds Out

By Suvashree Ghosh
October 19, 2026 at 8:00 PM GMT+8

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Multicoin Capital Management is resisting the rush into artificial intelligence, betting its expertise in digital assets gives it an edge in finding promising businesses.
The firm, which has $2.7 billion of assets under management, isn't broadening its mandate to cover standalone AI businesses, according to Spencer Applebaum, general partner and co-head of venture.
Multicoin's commitment to digital assets extends to its hedge fund, which buys cryptocurrencies directly, with its biggest position being HYPE, the cryptocurrency associated with decentralized derivatives exchange Hyperliquid.
Multicoin Capital Management is resisting the rush into artificial intelligence that has swept up rival crypto investment firms, betting its expertise in digital assets gives it an edge in finding promising businesses.

The Austin-based firm, which has $2.7 billion of assets under management, invests in startups and cryptocurrencies. It is taking longer to deploy its latest venture fund, raised in 2022, but isn’t broadening its mandate to cover standalone AI businesses, according to Spencer Applebaum, general partner and co-head of venture.

“We believe we have an edge in crypto, and we want to stay true to it,” Applebaum, who joined the firm in 2018, said in an interview with Bloomberg.

The strategy sets Multicoin apart in an industry facing difficulty raising fresh funds amid competition for investors’ money from AI. Paradigm, Framework Ventures Management and Haun Ventures have expanded their mandates beyond digital assets. Paradigm raised $1.2 billion this year for a fund whose remit includes AI and robotics.

A maturing crypto industry with fewer compelling investment opportunities has also encouraged investors to look elsewhere.

Funding for crypto startups is running at a similar pace to last year, with roughly $10 billion invested in the first half compared with $20 billion for all of 2025, according to Galaxy Research. But raising capital for new investment funds remains difficult. Investors allocated about $3.9 billion to five new crypto-focused venture funds in the second quarter, the fewest new funds raised since the last quarter of 2019, according to the research firm.

As speculative appetite for digital assets remained subdued for much of this year, retail and institutional money has flowed into AI. AI-focused companies captured roughly two-thirds of the capital invested in US and Canadian startups in the third quarter, according to Crunchbase.

Having never made a pure-play AI investment, though, Multicoin would lack the advantages it has in the crypto space, according to Applebaum. The company’s track record and relationships make it one of the first investors that entrepreneurs approach, he said.

“For the most part, people are in search of a problem that doesn’t exist at the intersection of crypto and AI,” he said. “A lot of investors are trying to force it.”
expected_focus: The supplied original discusses Multicoin rather than Jupiter: source_mismatch, not proof that all claims in the published copy are false.
